Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Medlytics - Technical deep dive (post-discovery) / scheduling

Hi Priya and Tom,

Thanks again for the discovery earlier — great conversation and really helpful context on Medlytics' inference needs. As discussed, the best next step is a technical deep dive (60–90 minutes) with your ML and infrastructure folks so our engineers can go over performance expectations, integration points, and deployment options.

Proposed agenda (draft):
- 5 min: quick intros and goals for the session
- 15 min: recap of current model architecture and key SLAs (latency, throughput) — Priya/Tom
- 30–45 min: Redwood technical walkthrough: serving runtime, quantization/compat options, routing/caching, expected throughput profiling
- 15 min: integration details: data paths, auth/KMS, logging/audit requirements
- 10–15 min: Q&A and next steps / mutual action plan

Suggested slots (PT):
- Mon 6/28: 1:00–2:30pm (90m)
- Tue 6/29: 10:00–11:30am (90m) or 2:00–3:00pm (60m)
- Wed 6/30: 9:00–10:30am (90m)

Can you confirm which of those works for your team and who from Medlytics will attend (ML lead, infra/ops, security if required)? I attached a mutual action plan with the high-level milestones.

I'll loop in our solutions engineer (Camila) to cover infra-specific items.

Thanks,

Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0172
Redwood Inference

Chloe —

Thanks, this looks good. We're keen to move forward. Our ML lead (Tom Nguyen) and our infra lead (Raj Patel, cc'd on internal side) should join; I'll confirm Raj but Tom and I can attend.

From our side the best slots are: Mon 6/28 1:00–2:30pm PT or Tue 6/29 2:00–3:00pm PT. Either works. Can you also share any pre-read or a short doc outlining the specific infra questions you want us to prepare for?

Also can you share the recording/transcript from today's discovery or any notes?

Chloe/Priya —

Confirming I can lead the technical deep dive on Mon 6/28 1:00–2:30pm PT. 90 minutes is ideal so we have time for hands-on profiling questions.

A few things I'll plan to cover and would appreciate if Priya/Tom can have answers prepared where possible:
- Model formats and sizes (FP32, FP16, quantized variants), number of parameters
- Typical sequence length distribution and peak request concurrency
- Target latency and p99 SLOs (ms/token or end-to-end)
- Any dataset redaction / PII concerns and requirements around data residency
- Authentication model (do you use customer KMS/HSM? SAML? OAuth?)

If you have a runbook or infra diagram, please share prior to the meeting — it'll help us tailor the demo to your environment. I'll also prepare a short perf profile of a similar model and options for quantization and caching.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
